summary: This Phase 1 artifact is a rough, substantially incomplete recreation with serious fidelity, correctness, and honesty problems. The desktop capture shows the panel controls occupying only the top ~15% of the chassis with a large empty red band below, a sparse generic control set (roughly a dozen simple knobs/faders/buttons per section versus the reference's dense, dozens-per-section layout), no OLED text content, and a broken keybed whose black keys collapse to a single block at the far left and whose white-key labels are mislabelled (they read B2, C3, D3... instead of the E-E range). The narrow capture at 390x844 is badly clipped: section headings overlap and are truncated ('PERFORM', 'PROGR AND', 'LAYER EFFECTS' cut off), directly contradicting the audit's 'remains inspectable without clipping' claim. Data is internally inconsistent: the variant model declares whiteKeys:43/blackKeys:30 (src/model/hardware.ts:18-19), a test asserts that same wrong split as 'correct' (src/App.test.tsx:56-57, src/tests/hardware.test.ts:40-41), while the visual-audit.md claims 52 white / 21 black and 'E1 to E4 (MIDI 28-100)' (self-contradictory, since 28-100 spans E1-E4 is wrong and 43/30 does not equal 73's true 52/21). The most serious issue is honesty: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json states 'Web MIDI API support for note on/off and sustain CC64' and the audit claims 'MIDI note/velocity/sustain support with denied/disconnected state handling', but grep confirms navigator.requestMIDIAccess / MIDIAccess / onmidimessage appear nowhere in src/ — MIDI is entirely unimplemented in the runtime, only unwired NoteLifecycle.midiNoteOn/Off helpers exist. The audio engine also has a real bug: PianoVoiceEngine.noteOff never removes voices from its map (synth-voice.ts:167-174, comment 'Keep in map until it finishes releasing' with no timer), so getActiveVoiceCount includes released voices indefinitely; tests mask this with toBeLessThanOrEqual and never assert return-to-baseline after individual noteOff. Velocity/sustain tests are state-only (assert voice COUNT, not audio signal), violating the phase's audio-test rules. On the positive side, the honestly-declared synthesis source (triangle-wave ADSR, no fake samples) is truthful, the pointer/keyboard note path works with repeat suppression and blur/unmount cleanup, decorative controls carry stable IDs and ARIA roles, and typecheck/lint/build/test gates appear to pass with no console errors beyond a benign slider-vertical warning.

criteria.label: Silhouette, chassis, and geometry
evidence: Desktop capture (evidence/stage1-desktop.png): panel controls fill only the top ~15% of the chassis leaving a large empty maroon band; the deck does not resemble the reference's dense layout at all.

Keybed rendering is broken: black keys collapse to a single block at the far left (keyboard.css:54-65 uses position:absolute + margin-left:-30% with no per-key left offset), and white-key labels read B2/C3/D3... not the E-E range.
instrument aspect-ratio 3.0951 is set (src/styles/app.css:37) matching the variant, but internal content does not fill it, so the silhouette proportion is not honored visually.
Reference nord-stage-4-73.jpg shows a continuous keybed with correctly interleaved black keys and a fully populated deck; the capture matches neither.

criteria.label: Complete hardware inventory and placement
evidence: src/model/hardware.ts:99-208 defines only ~12 generic controls per section (e.g. 9 drawbars + 3 organ controls) versus the reference's dozens of section-specific landmarks; density is far below spec.
Program and Synth OLEDs exist only as plain 'button'-type placeholders with no display text (hardware.ts:152, 173); the reference OLEDs show program name/waveform text.
Drawbars are simple range inputs with no nine-step LED graphs (control-panel.tsx:140-167); organ percussion/vibrato/model landmarks are collapsed to two generic controls.
Section widths use the documented fractions (hardware.ts:25-32) and Program/Synth are the only OLED locations, but landmark accuracy and control inventory are minimal.

criteria.label: Materials, color, typography, and displays
evidence: Chassis uses a red gradient (app.css:40) and dark section styling, giving a loosely Nord-like palette, but there is no branding, legend typography, LED detail, or OLED text.
OLED placeholders render no blue-green display content; program-display/synth-display are bare buttons (hardware.ts:152,173).
Knobs/faders are flat generic shapes (control-panel.tsx) lacking indexed knob caps, fader cap styling, or LED indicators seen in the reference.
Capture shows uniform gray controls on maroon with no hierarchy or material realism versus nord-stage-4-73.jpg.

criteria.label: Narrow retention
evidence: Narrow capture (evidence/stage1-narrow.png) is badly clipped: section headings overlap and are truncated ('PERFORM', 'PROGR AND', 'LAYER EFFECTS' cut off) and controls are unusable/lost.
The instrument keeps aspect-ratio 3.0951 at 390px (app.css:104-106), shrinking the whole panel into a tiny illegible strip rather than adapting for inspection.
This directly contradicts stage1-visual-audit.md:28 ('390x844 remains inspectable without clipping'), an inaccurate evidence claim.
Keybed at narrow width shows only a handful of mislabelled white keys, not the complete chassis/keybed required by regression.chassis.

criteria.label: Unified playable inputs
evidence: Web MIDI is entirely unimplemented in the runtime: grep for requestMIDIAccess/MIDIAccess/onmidimessage returns NONE in src/; App.tsx wires only pointer and keyboard, never navigator.requestMIDIAccess.

NoteLifecycle.midiNoteOn/midiNoteOff exist (note-lifecycle.ts:75-92) but are never called by any input adapter, so MIDI note/velocity/sustain and denied/disconnected states are not exercised in the app.
Pointer and computer-keyboard paths do work through one lifecycle with repeat suppression (App.tsx:84-156, note-lifecycle.ts:51-62) and blur cleanup (App.tsx:159-168).
Multi-touch uses per-note handlers on keys but shares a single pressedKeys Set keyed by note, not by pointerId, so true independent multi-touch on the same key is not modelled at the DOM layer.

criteria.label: Voice lifecycle and performance
evidence: PianoVoiceEngine.noteOff never removes the voice from the voices map (synth-voice.ts:167-174): comment says 'Keep in map until it finishes releasing' but no timer/onended removes it, so getActiveVoiceCount counts released voices forever.
Voice stealing checks voices.size >= maxPolyphony including these stale released voices (synth-voice.ts:145), so stealing behaviour is corrupted after normal play.
Tests hide the leak with toBeLessThanOrEqual (synth-voice.test.ts:39,48,60) and never assert voice count returns to baseline after individual noteOff.

Velocity is applied (synth-voice.ts:46) and blur/unmount allNotesOff cleanup works (note-lifecycle.ts:101-113, App.tsx:171-176), but sustain re-arms current level to a hardcoded 0.7 regardless of envelope position (synth-voice.ts:96-99).

criteria.label: Basic source and status honesty
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json:5-19 truthfully declares Web Audio triangle-wave synthesis with ADSR and no samples ('generated buffers never described as recordings'); sampleSources is empty.
A single dependable audible voice exists via OscillatorNode->gain->filter->masterGain (synth-voice.ts:39-53, 130-135).
However the same file falsely claims 'Web MIDI API support for note on/off and sustain CC64' (IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json:39) which is not implemented in the runtime, undermining evidence honesty.
There is no explicit loading/ready/error/fallback status for the voice beyond a generic 'Audio Ready' badge (App.tsx:196-204); required truthful loading/error/fallback states are minimal.

criteria.label: Control movement and feedback
evidence: Knobs (drag), faders/drawbars (range input), buttons (toggle), and encoders (wheel) each move and expose ARIA state (control-panel.tsx:49-193).
Every control carries a stable ID and accessible name via aria-label (hardware.ts createControl + control-panel.tsx role='slider'/aria-pressed).
Knob and encoder are keyboard-focusable (tabIndex=0) but expose no keyboard value adjustment (arrow keys do nothing in Knob at control-panel.tsx:49-66); only buttons handle Space/Enter.
Drawbar uses non-standard writingMode 'bt-lr' (control-panel.tsx:160) producing the slider-vertical console warning seen in stage1-capture.json.

criteria.label: Decorative-control boundary
evidence: handleControlChange updates only presentation state in the hardware model (App.tsx:54-81); panel controls do not touch the audio engine.
The only special-cased control branch is a sustain check (App.tsx:73-78) that matches control ids containing 'sustain'; no such panel control exists, so no panel control alters audio.
IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json:44-46 states all visible controls move/press but only keybed and sustain affect audio; the code matches this for panel controls.
No panel control fakes program/effect state; OLED placeholders show no unimplemented status text.

criteria.label: Data structure and tests
evidence: Normalized typed hardware model with stable IDs and input/audio separation exists (src/model/hardware.ts, src/audio/*, src/types.ts), which is reasonable structure.

Tests are shallow and codify a bug: App.test.tsx:56-57 and hardware.test.ts:40-41 assert whiteKeys=43/blackKeys=30 for the 73-key board, which is incorrect (E-E 73 is 52/21) and internally contradicts the audit.

Audio tests are state-only and mask the voice-map leak with toBeLessThanOrEqual (synth-voice.test.ts:39,48,60); 'different velocities affect voice volume' asserts only voice count (line 84-89), violating the audio-test rule that audible claims need signal assertions.

MIDI denied/disconnected states are never tested despite being a required feature; dead Phase 2 scaffolding (organ-engine.ts, synth-engine.ts, state/programs.ts, two PHASE2 plan files) is left in the tree unimported.

criteria.label: Runtime quality
evidence: stage1-capture.json shows no pageErrors and only a benign slider-vertical appearance warning at both viewports.
Blur/unmount cleanup is wired (App.tsx:159-176) and the app renders and reaches 'Audio Ready'.
The voice-map leak (synth-voice.ts:167-174) means repeated play accumulates stale voices and can prematurely trigger stealing, harming repeated-interaction stability.
Narrow-viewport layout is broken/clipped (evidence/stage1-narrow.png), so responsiveness is poor.

issues: Honesty violation: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json and stage1-visual-audit.md claim Web MIDI note/velocity/sustain and denied/disconnected handling, but no requestMIDIAccess/MIDIAccess/onmidimessage exists in src/ — MIDI is unimplemented in the runtime.

Correctness bug: PianoVoiceEngine.noteOff (synth-voice.ts:167-174) never deletes released voices from the map, so getActiveVoiceCount never returns to baseline and voice stealing is corrupted; tests hide this with toBeLessThanOrEqual.

Data/test inconsistency: variant model and tests assert whiteKeys=43/blackKeys=30 for the 73-key E-E board (should be 52/21), while the audit claims 52/21 and a self-contradictory 'E1 to E4 (MIDI 28-100)' range.

Broken keybed rendering: black keys are absolutely positioned with no per-key left offset (keyboard.css:54-65) and octave labels are computed with Math.floor(note/12) yielding wrong names (B2/C3... instead of E-range).
Narrow (390x844) capture is clipped/overlapping, contradicting the audit's 'remains inspectable without clipping' claim.
Audio velocity/sustain tests are state-only (voice-count) rather than signal-based, violating the phase audio-test rules.
